answer: An agent economy can require every participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable work bond before it may submit jobs, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fraudulent outputs. A single operator can still create many identities, but each one must tie up real capital and risk losing it; splitting a fixed budget across sybils also leaves each with less influence. Auditors can sample jobs across an island of agents, compare results along a ridge of repeated tasks, and use a copper token only as a receipt—not as proof of identity.
